editorial:
Imagine heading back to your childhood home not for a happy visit, but to completely crash your dad's new wedding. That is exactly what Sloane and her boyfriend Barrett are planning. You get to watch this tension build as they try to stir up trouble for Roan, the father who probably doesn't want them there. The vibe is very awkward and tense, like a family dinner where everyone is pretending to be nice while actually hating each other. It feels like a game of cat and mouse where no one is playing fair, and you will find yourself wondering who is actually the villain in this messy family dynamic.

The acting is great because the actors make the anger and sadness feel real. You will love the plot twists that keep you guessing about why the family is so broken. While the middle part slows down a bit, the payoff at the end makes it worth the wait. If you like stories about secrets and lies, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you want the best picture quality, grab the 4K Blu-ray to keep in your physical collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you find out that Sloane's plan to ruin the wedding was actually a way to force her father to admit to a huge lie about her mother. The twist reveals that Roan had been hiding a dark secret for years to protect his image. Once the truth comes out, the wedding falls apart. Sloane finally gets the closure she needed, and the movie ends with her leaving the house for good.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas and shocking secrets.
